description: Unfold's whole Renovate policy, with no shared preset. Third-party minor, patch, digest and pin updates share one branch that merges itself on green after a release-age soak; dependencies that never ship merge themselves in a branch of their own; security fixes merge themselves; majors, Go toolchain minors and the always-review list wait for a dashboard tick. platformAutomerge hands a green automerging pull request to the forge's own auto-merge.

vulnerabilityAlerts.description: Security fixes bypass the dashboard and open immediately. This block is the only thing that does so: "vulnerability" is not a valid matchUpdateTypes value, so a packageRule matching on it never fires. A consumer that wants these to merge themselves sets automerge here, not in packageRules, because this layer is applied on top of them. The fix strategy stays lowest on purpose: with automerge downstream, the smallest version that closes the CVE is the one you want, not the newest release.

prBodyNotes: {{#if isMajor}}⚠️ **Major update**: review upstream migration notes and rollout impact before merging.{{/if}}
{{#if isVulnerabilityAlert}}🔒 **Security update**: prioritize review and verify the vulnerable component is actually deployed.{{/if}}
{{#if isGroup}}📦 **Grouped update**: confirm the group is operationally coherent before merging.{{/if}}
Merge Confidence badges are included where supported — low or neutral confidence warrants a manual impact check before merge.

`Released` is the upstream publish time. `—` means the datasource reports no release timestamp. Docker Hub is the only Docker registry that reports one, so this preset treats every other Docker registry (ghcr.io, quay.io, dhi.io and registry proxies) as `timestamp-optional`: `minimumReleaseAge` cannot hold those updates back and they are eligible as soon as checks pass. For any other datasource, a missing timestamp holds the update for as long as a soak applies. A real date means the soak is enforced: add this update type's `minimumReleaseAge` to `Released` to get the eligibility moment.

customManagers.description: An agent package from the former host, such as agent-standards, pinned by a vX.Y.Z tag in apm.yml.
The agentstd CLI pinned to an agent-standards tag in mise.toml tasks, so the tool moves with the packages.

Update ARGs annotated with '# renovate: datasource=… depName=…'. The Dockerfiles compose their FROM refs from a registry variable and a digest-pinned tag, which the dockerfile manager cannot replace; tag and digest are captured separately so digest-pinned ARGs stay managed.

Local checks run the CI toolchain images by tag outside any workflow file. Managing them here keeps release-check and docs-site-check on the image CI uses; a package rule puts these updates on the branch that moves the workflow pins.
Composite actions take their BuildKit, SBOM scanner and binfmt images as `with:` strings, which the github-actions manager does not read. Tag and digest are captured so the digest stays managed.

The local MCP end-to-end compose file runs the Authentik that the nightly mcp-e2e job runs through Harbor's ghcr proxy. Naming the dependency after the workflow's image puts both pins in one update, so one pull request moves both; the proxy serves the upstream digest.
See the Authentik manager above: the compose file's Postgres moves with the nightly job's Postgres from Harbor's Docker Hub proxy.
The local agent image is tagged with the OpenCode version it carries. The example configurations and the live guide name that tag, so they move with the opencode group.

The agent sandbox warm pool and the live local example run the released unfold-agent image. Renovate moves them to the newest candidate the release pushed to Harbor, so they do not depend on a release commit to follow the release.
The landscape build loads Mermaid and Marked from jsDelivr inside Playwright.

Unfold depends on a released Ploeg (system ADR-0039). apps/unfold/ploeg-release.json pins Ploeg's contract bundle, an OCI artifact on GHCR, by version and digest; scripts/ploeg-contract.py unpacks it into apps/ploeg after checking both digests.

The agent-standards catalogue: every watch entry is one flow mapping on one line, {kind: K, ref: R, current: "V"}, which scripts/agent-standards.py enforces. Loose versioning because spec repositories tag however they like and an IETF revision is a bare number.

packageRules.description: Major updates: major label, plain feat commits. A dependency's major is not the product's major: a breaking marker on a dependency bump once cut a 1.0.0 candidate off a database image bump.
Minor updates — fix commits: a dependency's minor is not a feature of the consuming product, so it cuts a patch release, the same as a patch update.
Patch updates — fix commits
Digest-only updates — no changelog needed, chore commits
Pin Docker image digests
Pin GitHub Actions to immutable digests and treat workflow updates as CI-only

A pin of the former host's shared tooling in a file the repository never ships changes how the repository is built, not what it ships, so it lands as ci(tooling) whatever the update type and never cuts a release. Those files are the CI files (.forgejo/** and .github/**: reusable workflow and composite action refs, toolchain images) and mise.toml (a task that runs a toolchain image, a tool it installs). When these bumps landed as fix(deps), Unfold released for a tooling change. A package in a file that ships (package.json, a Dockerfile) keeps the commit type of its update type. The rule goes when those pins leave the repository.
Disable peer dependency updates to avoid range-only churn

Never digest-pin mise-managed tools. The mise manager cannot write digests into .mise.toml aqua/backend entries — the replace never applies ('Digest is not updated') and, like the preset-reference case above, the single failed dep aborts the whole grouped branch ('Error updating branch: update failure' on renovate/mise-tools). Version pins remain enabled.

Never digest-pin an action's version input (`with: version:`, depType uses-with). The value is handed to the action, which cannot take a digest. The digest lookup searches for the tag without its v prefix, fails ('Could not determine new digest for update'), and drops the update silently: Unfold sat on mise 2026.6.14 while 2026.9.17 shipped.

Renovate defaults to minimumReleaseAgeBehaviour timestamp-required, which silently keeps an update without a release timestamp out of every branch for as long as a soak applies. Only Docker Hub reports Docker release timestamps, so images from any other registry were detected and never proposed wherever an overlay restores the soak. These registries cannot report a timestamp; the soak is skipped for them because it cannot be measured, not because it is unwanted.
Require explicit dashboard approval for all normal updates
Docker updates wait for a tick, digest pins included.
CI action updates wait for a tick, digest pins included.
The tick is the gate, so ticked update types carry no release-age soak; the non-major part restores it where it lifts the tick.

Every pin of an agent package installs with agentstd, so the lockfile and the generated agent files arrive in the bump's pull request. A bump of agent files changes what agents read, not what the repository ships, so it lands as chore(agents) and cuts no release.
A bump of agent-standards installs with the CLI from the tag it bumps to, so the lockfile and the generated agent files match that release.

Minor, patch and pin updates share one branch and open without a dashboard tick. One pull request per run instead of one per dependency: every open branch costs a CI run each time it is rebased. A branch that waits for a person rebases only on a conflict: with behind-base-branch every push to the base branch would rebase it and rerun its CI. Branches that merge themselves set behind-base-branch, because a red result from an old base would otherwise keep them from merging forever.
Without the tick the soak returns, so a freshly published release is not proposed the hour it appears.
Patch soak without the tick.

Non-major updates share one branch and merge themselves once its checks are green. One grouped branch per run instead of one per dependency: every open branch costs a full CI run each time it is rebased, and a small runner pool cannot absorb twenty of them per push. The branch rebases when it falls behind, at most once per Renovate run.
With minor and patch combined, Renovate offers only the highest non-major Go version, a minor that waits for approval, so the toolchain patch would never be proposed. Go keeps them apart.

A Go toolchain minor decides what compiles the shipped binaries and raises the floor for contributors. It stays a deliberate, dashboard-approved change outside the group; toolchain patches still merge themselves. The tick is its gate, so it carries no soak: a tick on an update still inside its soak is discarded.
Go toolchain patches merge themselves in their own branch: kept apart from minors, they cannot share the non-major group's branch.
Indirect Go modules share one branch. The golang overlay enables them; this rule only decides where they land.

golang.org/x modules share one branch whether they are direct or indirect. They cut releases in lockstep, share go.sum entries, and `go mod tidy` resolves them together, so one pull request per module only rebases the others for no review value.

Always review: libraries that hold credentials, sign or verify tokens, or speak to the database. A green test suite rarely covers a changed token check or connection default, so their minor, patch and digest updates wait for a dashboard tick in a branch of their own. The tick is their gate, so they carry no soak: a tick on an update still inside its soak is discarded. Only where they ship: as a devDependency or require-dev they fall to the never-ships rules below.

Never ships: npm devDependencies and Composer require-dev, which is where linters, formatters, test runners and type packages live. They are not installed in what a repository deploys, so a green CI run is the whole question; their minor, patch and pin updates share a branch of their own that merges itself after the soak, apart from the branch a person merges. A database driver used only by tests is one of them: the always-review rule excludes these dependency types.
Never ships: type packages carry no runtime code, whichever dependency list they sit in.

Packages from the former host (its registry project, its npm scope and its repositories) share one branch that merges itself on green without a soak. They include the unfold-agent image references, which must move on a branch of their own kind rather than with third-party updates. The rule goes when those pins leave the repository.
A major of a package from the former host opens its pull request without a dashboard tick and never merges itself; the major's branch, commit type and zero soak stay as the earlier rules set them.
The annotated-ARG manager owns the composed base images and the opencode pin.
Bare versions are reused outside the FROM line; digests are captured explicitly.

Forgejo-resolved workflow pins keep the CI-only commit shape. A runner-level Forgejo overlay sets it too, but runner-level config is applied before the per-update-type commit types above, which then win.

The agent image and the mise pin must move together: one OpenCode version is what the workbench, the probe and the image share. The npm package names no repository, so Renovate cannot find its release notes by itself; naming the source puts them in the pull request, where the person merging and the Run that explains the update (Ploeg ADR-0106) read them.

Moving Mermaid or Marked in the landscape build makes docs/landscape/explorer.html stale, and the docs gate stays red until someone rebuilds it with Playwright's Chromium, which Renovate's runner lacks. In the all non-major branch that red held every other update back (#839), so these pins get a branch of their own.
prBodyNotes: This update stays red until the landscape explorer is rebuilt: run `mise run landscape` on this branch and push the two changed files under `docs/landscape/`. Forgejo then merges it on a green gate.

packageRules.description: Every Unfold release is a candidate X.Y.Z-rc.N, so the released unfold-agent image is offered as one. Moving the references releases nothing: a releasing commit type would cut a candidate whose image Renovate then offers again. A reference ahead of Harbor is a release still publishing, not one to roll back.

engines ranges are compatibility floors, not dependencies. Pinning or bumping engines.vscode narrows which VS Code builds the extension installs on, and engines.node is the deliberate Node 24 line. Both move by hand.
vsce refuses to package when @types/vscode is newer than engines.vscode (^1.99.0). Raise this bound together with engines.vscode.
Unfold's chart image tag is empty on purpose: the release train fills it from appVersion. Renovate would otherwise digest-pin it.

Ploeg's release workflow opens the Ploeg pull request by running scripts/consume-ploeg-release.sh (ADR-0041), so Renovate leaves the contract bundle pin, the Go module and the Unfold chart's ploeg dependency alone (ADR-0043): two writers on one pin would race. The weekly ploeg-behind check fails when the pin falls behind Ploeg's newest release.
These pins replace the copies npm bundles in the agent image, and the patch script accepts only the bundled major. Raise the bound when npm bundles a newer major.
See the undici rule: brace-expansion is pinned to npm's bundled major.
Node types follow the Node 24 runtime that mise, engines and the images pin.
@astrojs/check and typescript-eslint accept TypeScript up to 6. Lift this when both peer ranges include 7.
three is vendored into apps/unfold/public/vendor/three (Unfold ADR-0028). A version bump alone breaks the vendored copy's checks; upgrade by hand with npm run vendor:three.
uv runs every docs gate, and a 0.x minor may break: uv 0.13 made Python 3.15 the default (dependency intake of #351). A person reviews each 0.x minor before it merges.

pnpm 11 and later keep the pnpm that packageManager names in the lockfile's first document (packageManagerDependencies), and a frozen install refuses a lockfile whose record disagrees. The self-hosted Renovate image runs its own global pnpm, which switches to the packageManager version with package-manager management turned off, so that record keeps the old version (#593, fixed by hand in #596). Corepack runs exactly the pnpm packageManager names, as CI does, and that pnpm rewrites the record. The homelab's allowedCommands must list this command; docs/operations/ci-troubleshooting.md has the entry.

Lock-file maintenance regenerates a pnpm lockfile with the same global pnpm, which drops the lockfile's first document and with it the packageManagerDependencies record a frozen install needs (#784). The same corepack command restores it. The rule names each pnpm project, because in an npm project the command would write a stray pnpm-lock.yaml.

The tooling rules above give pins of the former host's packages under .forgejo/** their own webgrip CI dependencies branch, committed as ci(tooling). The local-check pins of the same images sit in mise.toml and scripts/docs-site.sh, outside that rule, so they moved on a separate fix(deps) branch: development then ran the release jobs on the new semantic-release image while release-check still named the old one, and the workflow policy test failed the release. This rule moves both on one branch, and the ci type keeps that branch from cutting a release.

Pins of the former host's packages in files the repository never ships (CI files and mise.toml) share one branch, majors included. Renovate gives a branch the highest commit type among its updates (fix beats ci), so a branch shared with anything that ships would commit these pins as fix(deps) and cut a release. separateMajorMinor is off for these pins, so each pin moves straight to the newest release instead of splitting into two branches that conflict. A branch that holds a major waits for a person.

One pull request per agent package bumps every pin of that package together (apm.yml and the agentstd tag in mise.toml), so the generated files and the lockfile move in one step. The tooling rule turns separateMajorMinor off for pins in mise.toml and comes earlier, so this rule turns it back on.

A watched agent standard is not a dependency: its pull request asks whether a radar ring moves, so it never merges on its own, needs no soak, and stays one pull request per standard. The docs type keeps it from cutting a release.
prBodyNotes: This bumps a watched standard in apps/unfold/docs/research/agent-standards/standards.yaml. Before merging, read the release notes, update latest, status and reviewed, decide whether the radar ring moves, re-read the decisions the entry names, then run mise run agent-standards and commit the regenerated pages. The procedure is docs/how-to/keep-the-agent-standards-catalogue-current.md.
